metadata.title: CrowdStrike’s Zscaler deal sets up Palo Alto rivalry, R.F. Lafferty analyst says

content.text:
Investing.com -- CrowdStrike's (NASDAQ: CRWD) planned $43.9 billion acquisition of Zscaler (NASDAQ: ZS) is a positive that could give it a product range to rival Palo Alto Networks (NASDAQ: PANW), Paul Rodriguez, senior research analyst at R.F. Lafferty & Co., told Investing.com.
Under the all-stock deal, Zscaler shareholders will receive 1.135 CrowdStrike shares for each share they own. That implies about $260.41 per share, a premium of roughly 34% to Zscaler's Nov. 20 close.
If approved, the deal is expected to close in the second half of CrowdStrike's fiscal 2028.
"Cyber consolidation has reached the point where customers are demanding consolidation. CrowdStrike has been keeping close tabs on Palo Alto Networks and may feel it has to 'bulk up' as the AI Security opportunity becomes a reality," Rodriguez said.
He added that Palo Alto's strategy of offering security chiefs a one-stop shop had worked, and that CrowdStrike was looking to replicate it.
"CrowdStrike's strength around SecOps (especially its SIEM solution) paired with ZS's expertise in SASE, would result in a platform that rivals Palo Alto Networks product breadth," the analyst argues.
CrowdStrike expects about $1 billion in annualized revenue synergies within 30 months of closing and $500 million in annual cost savings within 18 to 24 months. The combined company is expected to start with more than $10 billion in annual recurring revenue.
Rodriguez also highlighted Zscaler's international reach.
"ZS had strong channels in EMEA and Asia-Pacific, which will be additive to CrowdStrike in those geographic theaters," he said. "With Zscaler, CrowdStrike can become even more of a strategic vendor to clients as opposed to a tactical vendor."
